persona.name: Martine
persona.background: Daughter of a Manufrance factory worker and a mother at home; 15 in 1968. Music came from the family transistor tuned to Europe n°1 for 'Salut les copains' at 5 pm, RTL, the monthly SLC magazine, 45s on a Teppaz record player shared with her older brother, the juke-box at the café on the corner, 'Âge tendre et tête de bois' on ORTF, and the accordion bal on 14 July.

seeds.song: Michel Polnareff - La poupée qui fait non
Jacques Dutronc - Et moi, et moi, et moi
France Gall - Poupée de cire, poupée de son
Sylvie Vartan - La plus belle pour aller danser
Françoise Hardy - Tous les garçons et les filles
Richard Anthony - J'entends siffler le train
Procol Harum - A Whiter Shade of Pale
The Rolling Stones - (I Can't Get No) Satisfaction

FR1968A.wouldSay: Polnareff, puis Dutronc ! C'est 'Salut les copains', ça — on écoutait ça en rentrant du collège. Mais où est 1968 ? On dirait 1965.
missing: Jacques Dutronc - Il est cinq heures, Paris s'éveille (1968)
Joe Dassin - Siffler sur la colline (1968)
FR1968A.fake: Nothing is actually from 1967–68: it stops at the 1962–66 yé-yé years, so it sounds like my older brother's youth rather than the year I was fifteen.

seeds.song: Édith Piaf - Non, je ne regrette rien
Françoise Hardy - Comment te dire adieu
Borodin Quartet - Shostakovich: String Quartet No. 8
Columbia Symphony Orchestra, Igor Stravinsky - Stravinsky: The Rite of Spring

FR1968B.wouldSay: Aznavour, Brel, Brassens, Piaf… c'est la France des parents, celle des cartes postales. Et après, Chostakovitch et de la musique concrète ? Personne n'écoutait ça chez nous.
missing: Michel Polnareff - La poupée qui fait non (1966)
Jacques Dutronc - Il est cinq heures, Paris s'éveille (1968)
Procol Harum - A Whiter Shade of Pale (1967)
FR1968B.fake: Half of it is a conservatoire syllabus (Ives, Shostakovich, Stravinsky, GRM musique concrète) and the rest is the tourist chanson canon plus prewar musette, with almost none of the yé-yé or foreign pop a teenager actually heard on Europe n°1. Unsure: the first disc release date of Parmegiani's 'Capture éphémère' (composed 1967).

persona.name: Javier
persona.background: Son of a CASA aircraft-factory worker from Jaén and a mother who cleaned houses; 13 in 1980. Music came from Los 40 Principales on Cadena SER, the kitchen radio on Radio Nacional, TVE's 'Aplauso' on Saturdays, the rumba cassettes his father bought at petrol stations for the Seat 124 on the summer drive to the pueblo, the verbenas in August, and 'Grease' at the local cinema.

seeds.song: Las Grecas - Te estoy amando locamente
Camarón de la Isla - La Leyenda del Tiempo
Camarón de la Isla - Volando voy

ES1980A.wouldSay: ¡Los Chunguitos y Manzanita! Esto es la cinta de gasolinera que ponía mi padre en el coche camino del pueblo. Pero, ¿y Camilo Sesto, y Bosé? Esto es solo una parte.
missing: Camilo Sesto - Vivir así es morir de amor (1978)
Pink Floyd - Another Brick in the Wall (Part 2) (1979)
ES1980A.fake: It plays only the rumba-and-flamenco corner of 1980 (with Camarón's 1979 album, a commercial flop at the time, treated as a hit) plus a New York salsa track nobody here knew, and misses the ballads and pop that filled Los 40 Principales.

ES1980B.wouldSay: ¡Me quedo contigo! Y Camilo Sesto, y el Truhán de Julio… esto sonaba en la radio de la cocina de mi madre todos los días. Esto es mi infancia.
ES1980B.fake: Only that it leans on 1973–78 hits; almost nothing sounds like 1980 itself (no Bosé, Pecos, Tequila or Miguel Ríos), and 'Chica de ayer' was not yet the anthem it later became.

persona.name: Ewa
persona.background: Daughter of two textile-mill workers; 14 in 1975. Music came from Polskie Radio Program I and Trójka ('Lato z radiem'), the Opole and Sopot festivals on TVP every summer, Polskie Nagrania LPs and pocztówki dźwiękowe bought at kiosks, prywatki with a borrowed Unitra tape recorder, and Radio Luxembourg late at night through the crackle.

seeds.song: Deep Purple - Smoke on the Water

PL1975A.wouldSay: To jest jakaś zachodnia stacja… Deep Purple chłopaki puszczali, owszem, ale gdzie są nasi? Gdzie Jantar, gdzie Rodowicz? I skąd tu argentyńskie tango?
missing: Anna Jantar - Tyle słońca w całym mieście (1974)
Czesław Niemen - Dziwny jest ten świat (1967)
Skaldowie - Wszystko mi mówi, że mnie ktoś pokochał (1969)
PL1975A.fake: Not one Polish song: it is a Western radio list plus an Argentine tango, with 'The Hustle' a 1975 US disco record that had not reached a Łódź teenager that year.

PL1975B.wouldSay: Jarocka! A potem Budka i Jantar, 'Tyle słońca'… to było lato z radiem i Opole w telewizorze. Tak, to moja młodość.
missing: Trzy Korony / Krzysztof Klenczon - 10 w skali Beauforta (c.1970)
PL1975B.fake: Little feels fake; it leans on 1967–74 Opole classics and leaves out Czerwone Gitary, the band every school dance played. Unsure of exact years for Ada Rusowicz and Klenczon.

persona.name: Lerato
persona.background: Daughter of a domestic worker in the northern suburbs and a bus driver; 15 in 1988, during the State of Emergency. Music came from Radio Metro and Radio Zulu/Radio Setswana, TV2/TV3 and 'Ezodumo' on Sunday, cassettes from street hawkers and the taxi rank, street bashes and stokvel parties, the church choir, and her uncle's reggae records.

seeds.song: Johnny Clegg & Savuka - Scatterlings of Africa
Yvonne Chaka Chaka - I'm in Love with a DJ
Chris de Burgh - The Lady in Red

ZA1988A.wouldSay: Who is this singing in Afrikaans? … Ah, Clegg, and Lucky Dube 'Slave' — that one played at every bash. But where is Brenda? She should be first.
missing: Mahlathini and the Mahotella Queens - Thokozile (1987)
Paul Simon & Ladysmith Black Mambazo - Homeless (1986)
ZA1988A.fake: It opens with white-campus protest rock — Kerkorrel's 'Hillbrow' (on Eet Kreef, 1989 per the SAHA archive, so after 1988) and Bright Blue — before the bubblegum and mbaqanga we actually played, and later adds a David Kramer Afrikaans song no township kid knew. Unsure of the year of Kekana's 'The Bushman'.

ZA1988B.wouldSay: Mambazo — that's my grandfather's Sunday radio, and the Paul Simon song everybody talked about. But then this jazz from overseas? This is not what we danced to.
missing: Yvonne Chaka Chaka - I'm in Love with a DJ (1985)
ZA1988B.fake: It is the Graceland-and-world-music-shop South Africa — three Mambazo tracks, exiled jazz the SABC never played, a British compilation LP listed as a song, Rebecca Malope before she was famous (she only won Shell Road to Fame in 1987) — with no bubblegum at all, which was the actual sound of 1988.
